contextual_exceptions.rationale: The provided context documents this gradient as a brand requirement for the wordmark and main headline, which is exactly where it appears. It also falls short of VIS-02 on its own terms: a single occurrence, not a device repeated across sections, and its sunrise colors relate to the festival's name.

quality_observations.observation: The gradient heading has low contrast against the cream page background. Sampled glyph colors run from about rgb(255,137,0) at the left to rgb(255,93,52) at the right, against a background of rgb(255,250,243), giving roughly 2.3:1 to 2.9:1, below the WCAG 2.x AA 3:1 minimum for large text. This is an accessibility observation, not a slop claim, and it does not change X001.

consequence.reason: The heading remains legible in the screenshot at this size, but contrast is under the large-text threshold across all visible glyphs and may hinder low-vision readers.

summary.text: No accepted findings. The page's main surface cue, a gradient-filled headline (#hero > h1, computed orange rgb(255,138,0) to pink rgb(255,45,111)), is recorded as a contextual exception: the provided brand constraint requires that sunrise gradient on the wordmark and main headline, it is used only on the headline, and its colors fit the festival name. The copy is specific (named acts per day; June 11-13, which fall on Friday to Sunday in 2027 as the lineup says; Harbor Lawn; Pier Street station; $45 day passes), the section order fits an event announcement, and captured styles show no cards, decorative objects, or configured animation. Separately, as quality observations rather than slop claims: the gradient heading measures roughly 2.3:1 to 2.9:1 against the cream background, below the 3:1 large-text minimum, and because the gradient spans the full-width heading box, the glyphs show only its orange-to-red-orange half. Evidence is a single desktop viewport with no interactions or source.
major_limitations: Single desktop viewport (1280x800) at scroll 0; no mobile viewport, scroll states, or full-page capture. Visible content ends near y=495px, but anything below the first viewport is unknown.
No interactions or source excerpts, so INT-01, INT-02, and SRC-01 are unassessed.
Page or body background styles were not captured; the background color and contrast ratios come from sampling screenshot pixels and are approximate.
The exception rests on the provided context constraint; the page's own statement (T009) is used only as corroboration.
